standard_prerequisites.name: Linearised operator symbol and its low-frequency limit
standard_prerequisites.statement: The symbol is an integral transform of the background, and its limit as the parameter tends to zero is an explicit integral transform evaluated at zero parameter.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two objects on which the sign conditions are imposed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Uniform Penrose condition
standard_prerequisites.statement: The uniform Penrose condition requires that the real part of the symbol stay above a negative bound uniformly in the parameter, the spectral variable and the frequency direction.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the conclusion of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Analyticity and the argument principle
standard_prerequisites.statement: The symbol is analytic in the half-plane of the spectral variable, and a curve lying in the image of the imaginary axis that avoids a half-line bounds the argument of the relevant factor.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the mechanism that converts the sign condition into the bound.

core_obligations: Use the assumptions on the background to see that the symbol is analytic in the half-plane and that the image curve of the imaginary axis avoids the half-line of negative real parts below minus one (source lines 1148-1152).

Apply the argument principle to the factor obtained by adding one to the symbol, and conclude that its real part stays above a negative bound uniform in the parameter and the frequency (source line 1152).

Show that the infimum appearing in the uniform Penrose condition is positive: rewrite the symbol through the integral representation, introduce the auxiliary function of the rescaled variables, and bound the tail of its defining integral by splitting the range and using the third part of the boundedness and decay lemma (source lines 1154-1180).

proof_roadmap.step: Analyticity plus avoidance of the half-line, then the argument principle for the shifted factor.
Rescale the symbol through the integral representation and introduce the auxiliary function.
Bound the tail of the defining integral and conclude positivity of the infimum.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 1139-1146: if the imaginary part of the symbol vanishes only where its real part exceeds minus one, both for the symbol and for its low-frequency limit, then the uniform Penrose condition holds. The proof (source lines 1147-1189) first converts the pointwise sign condition into a statement about a curve in the complex plane and applies the argument principle to the symbol shifted by one, which is what produces a lower bound uniform in the parameter and the frequency; the positivity of the infimum in the condition is then established separately by rescaling the integral representation through an auxiliary function of the rescaled variables and bounding the tail of its defining integral with the third part of the boundedness and decay lemma. The statement records the two implications and the conclusion, and neither the curve argument nor the tail estimate.
